name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a thick, high-contrast focus ring to every interactive element that can be reached with the keyboard. This makes it obvious where the focus is, which is critical for keyboard users and people with low vision or motor control issues. The trade-off is a slight visual clutter for sighted mouse users, but the benefit to accessibility far outweighs this minor aesthetic cost.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s focus ring risks hiding content on small screens or cramped layouts, making it harder for *all* users—not just keyboard users—to see what’s behind it. Instead, pair a thin, high-contrast outline with a 2px offset shadow that doesn’t overlap adjacent elements; test it on a 320px mobile viewport and confirm no content is obscured. Settle it by measuring task completion time for keyboard users with and without the shadow—if the shadow wins, adopt it; if not, revert to the outline alone.
